newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Schengen spreads wings to Nordic countries.
newsitem.headline: Schengen spreads wings to Nordic countries.

text.p: The Schengen agreement -- Europe's most ambitious border-free pact yet -- spread to the five countries of the Nordic Passport Union on Thursday.
At a special ceremony the 10-nation group signed accession pacts with EU members Denmark, Finland and Sweden and cooperation pacts with Norway and Iceland, who are not EU members.
"It's a determining moment in the history of Schengen," Luxembourg's Justice Minister Marc Fischbach said at the signing.
"The Schengen space will now stretch as far as the eastern frontier of Finland to the Atlantic and the Mediterranean."

He admitted that the signing would not have an immediate impact for travellers from other Schengen countries -- Austria, France, Germany, Portugal, Spain, Luxembourg, Belgium, the Netherlands, Italy and Greece.
The new countries might not actually apply the deal until 1999 or 2000, he said, as ways would have to be found to integrate them into the already overloaded Schengen Information System computer.
